records.name: Volunteer at a prison
records.summary: Trains approved volunteers to offer educational or spiritual support to people held in one of the four Philadelphia Department of Prisons facilities.
records.what_you_do: After approval and 16 hours of training, volunteers give educational or spiritual support inside one of the four city facilities. A background check is required before you start.

schedule.text: Volunteers start once they are approved and finish training. The page gives no set weekly times.

locations.label: One of four Philadelphia Department of Prisons facilities: Curran-Fromhold, the Detention Center, Philadelphia Industrial Correctional Center, or Riverside

first_step.how: Email the completed volunteer application to pdp.volunteer@prisons.phila.gov. The form is a PDF linked from the city's volunteer form page.
first_step.basis: Volunteer Services reviews every application and accepts only people whose skills fit a current program need. Accepted applicants then complete training and a background check before they start.
first_step.what_to_expect: Accepted volunteers first finish 16 hours of training at the Department of Prisons training academy, which contacts them to begin a background check. After that, volunteers give educational or spiritual support inside a facility. The site does not describe a typical first visit or how often training classes run.
first_visit_tips: Check the rules first: applicants must be 21 or older with a valid state ID, and anyone who was incarcerated must wait six months after release.
If a relative is held in the system, say so on the application. You will not be placed at the facility where that relative is held.
General volunteer questions go to 215-685-8149. Religious volunteer questions go to 215-685-8385.

records.notes: The form page does not say where to send the form; the email comes from the service page. The earlier 2025-04 date was corrected to March 2025, when the form was released. The training academy location and how often classes run are not stated on any page read.

records.name: Vox Populi Gallery
records.summary: An artist-run gallery in North Chinatown with exhibitions, performances, film screenings and community events. It also runs open calls for artists and offers space rentals.
records.what_you_do: Visit during open hours, or come to an opening, performance or screening. Artists can apply to open calls, and supporters can give monthly through the Vox Circle or join the board.

schedule.text: Hours: Thursdays 4 to 6 pm, and Fridays through Sundays noon to 6 pm. Visits at other times can be booked by appointment.

cost.text: The site does not state an admission price for open hours. Some events are ticketed, and optional giving to the Vox Circle starts at $5 a month.

access.notes: Reaching the first floor landing takes five steps from the street, and the passenger elevator starts there. Its door is 29 inches wide, so it may not fit every wheelchair or motorized chair. The third floor has no further steps. A ramp is available if you contact the gallery ahead. Personal care attendants and service animals are welcome. The restroom door is 34 inches wide and has grab bars, but the page does not say whether the restroom is step free.

first_step.how: Come during open hours: Thursdays 4 to 6 pm, or Fridays through Sundays noon to 6 pm. The website also has a mailing list sign-up, but the page does not say whether you need it to visit.
first_step.basis: Open to the public on set days, with a clear events calendar and a mailing list. Internships, board seats and open calls are listed, but no beginner or volunteer program is.
first_step.what_to_expect: Open hours let you see the current exhibition on the third floor, which runs October 2 to November 15, 2026. The site does not state an admission charge for open hours. Performances and screenings have their own times, and some are ticketed.
first_visit_tips: If you need the ramp, call 215-238-1236 or email events@voxpopuligallery.org before you come.
Check the events page for performances and screenings, which have their own times and tickets.
The gallery spaces use window air conditioners, not central air.
To visit outside open hours, email director@voxpopuligallery.org to book an appointment.

records.notes: The visit page lists director@voxpopuligallery.org for appointments. The general address stays as the main email. Open calls, one-off events and partner presenters are recorded only as leads, since their dates change.

records.name: Affirming Hearts Academy (Mazzoni Center)
records.summary: A free group of eight sessions for LGBTQ+ adults, 18 and older, about healthy and affirming relationships. It looks at romantic, friendship, family and work connections.
records.what_you_do: Join the eight-session group to talk about what healthy relationships look like, using discussion and creative art. Participants receive journals, art supplies, SEPTA passes and snacks.

schedule.text: Runs as a set of eight sessions. The page does not give meeting days or times.

cost.text: Free. Journals, art supplies, SEPTA passes and snacks are provided.

first_step.how: Fill out the interest form linked on the group's page. The next group was listed to start September 22, 2026. For general questions, call the Bainbridge main line.
first_step.basis: Joining goes through an interest form, and the page gives no meeting days or times yet.
first_step.what_to_expect: The eight sessions mix talk, discussion and creative art about healthy relationships, including romantic, friendship, family and work connections. Topics include consent, communicating needs, boundaries and identity. The page does not say how long a session lasts, what day it meets, or how many people attend.
first_visit_tips: Ask for the meeting days and times when you send the interest form, since the page does not list them.
Ask how the SEPTA passes and snacks are handed out, since the page does not say.
The group is for LGBTQ+ adults 18 and older, so check that you qualify before you sign up.

records.notes: This record covers three Mazzoni programs listed in its aliases, and it should be split. Affirming Hearts Academy (this record): adult LGBTQ+ group, next start September 22, 2026, no days or times on its page. W.I.S.E. Aging and HIV Peer Resource Group (its own page): Tuesdays 1 to 3 pm, September 22 to November 10, 2026, sign-ups due September 15. LEAD Health Advocacy Group (its own page): LGBTQ+ youth ages 18 to 24, Tuesdays 5:30 to 7 pm, next cohort starting Tuesday, September 1, 2026, interest form. The earlier Tuesday evening schedule matches LEAD, so it appears to have come from the wrong program and was removed here. No new ids were created for W.I.S.E. or LEAD.

records.name: W.O.R.X. (Works of Raphael Xavier)
records.summary: A nonprofit that brings arts training to young people, with a focus on Breaking, the dance form from hip hop culture. It runs youth programs, often with local schools, and hosts community jams.
records.what_you_do: Young people take part in music, dance, theater and live skills programs, often through local schools. Community members can attend the Core Creek Flatland Jam, with riding, dancing, games and a cookout.

schedule.text: Youth programming runs through the year, with no weekly times on the page. Community jams are one-off events.

locations.label: Core Creek Park Pavilion #11 (site of the 2026 jam)

cost.text: Community jams have been free, with donations accepted. No other costs are listed.

first_step.how: Watch the group's site for the next community jam, which is open to the public. To ask about youth programs, use the Contact link on the site, since no email or phone is listed.
first_step.basis: Events are open to the public, and the page says the group welcomes families and newcomers to them. The page does not say how a young person joins a youth program.
first_step.what_to_expect: A community jam is held outdoors in a park pavilion, with riding, dancing, games and a cookout. The 2026 jam was held in June. The page does not say how long the day runs or how youth enroll in programs.
first_visit_tips: The 2026 jam was in Langhorne, Pennsylvania, outside Philadelphia, so plan on a drive.
The page does not list the date of the next jam, so check the site before you plan a trip.
For youth programs, ask through the site's contact page, since the page lists no email or phone.

records.notes: The Philadelphia link is not shown on the group's own site. The only 2026 event on the site is in Langhorne, Bucks County. The site lists past events at City Hall (2016) and the Kimmel Center (2017), and its founder lives in Philadelphia, but it gives no Philadelphia address or youth program. A web search found no Philadelphia youth program under this name, and a 2016 grant record spells the name 'Work'. A reviewer should decide between publish (kept from tier 1) and out_of_area before release. Youth program enrollment and contact details are not on the site.

records.name: Washington Square West Civic Association
records.summary: The civic association for the Washington Square West neighborhood. It runs three community gardens and co-hosts Open Garden Days with Farm Philly, the city's gardening program.
records.what_you_do: Come to the monthly board meeting, which is open to the public, or attend a garden day. Membership joins and renewals are handled online.

schedule.text: Board of Directors meetings are held on the second Tuesday of each month at 7 pm and are open to the public. The site does not give the meeting room.

cost.text: The site does not list dues. Joining and renewing happen through an online form.

first_step.how: Attend the board meeting on the second Tuesday at 7 pm. The site does not name the room, so call or email the association first to confirm where it meets.
first_step.basis: Board meetings are open to anyone and membership joins online, but the meeting room is not on the site, so the first visit takes one call or email.
first_step.what_to_expect: The board meeting is a public monthly meeting on the second Tuesday at 7 pm. The site does not describe the agenda or how long the meeting runs. Garden days are a hands-on way to meet the association's volunteers, and the association co-hosts them with Farm Philly.
first_visit_tips: Call 267-603-1318 or email info@washwestcivic.org to confirm the meeting room. The phone line is voicemail only.
The contact page lists an office at 1100 Walnut, Room B113, but the site does not say board meetings happen there.
Renters can join, and membership is handled through an online form. The site does not list dues.
Ask about the next Open Garden Day, which the association co-hosts with Farm Philly.

records.notes: The calendar page lists no 2026 events. Its news posts date from 2022 and 2023 and were not used as evidence. The earlier 2026-10 sign of life came from a zoning registry record, which shows registration rather than activity, so it was replaced with the May 2026 Open Garden Day. The Love Your Park listing does not say whether the garden days are open to the public. The membership benefits page returned 404. The 1100 Walnut office address is on the contact page only and is not confirmed as a meeting room.

records.name: South Street Community Garden
records.summary: One of the Washington Square West Civic Association's community gardens, at 839 South St. Plots go to people whose primary home is in the neighborhood, and the waitlist can be very long.
records.what_you_do: Plot holders follow the association's garden rules. The association also holds Open Garden Days here, and you can find them through its site or Love Your Park listings.

cost.text: The waitlist page does not list fees.

first_step.how: If your primary home is in Washington Square West, use the waitlist link on the association's community garden page and choose a first and second garden. Otherwise, watch for an Open Garden Day.
first_step.basis: Plots go to residents from a waitlist that the page says can take three years. Open Garden Days are the only visit route, and the listings do not say whether they are open to the public.
first_step.what_to_expect: Plots here go to residents of the neighborhood through a waitlist, and the page says some people wait three years. The association held an Open Garden Day at this garden on May 9, 2026, from 10 am to 2 pm during Love Your Park Week. The garden page does not describe a usual work day.
first_visit_tips: When you apply, pick a first and second choice garden. You are added to both waitlists.
The association defines the neighborhood as the area bounded by Market, Broad, South and 7th Streets. If you live close by but outside it, check the FAQ.
The garden page mentions garden rules without linking them, so ask the association for a copy.

records.notes: The record id says Waverly Street, but the address is South Street Garden at 831 to 839 South St. The association lists Sartain (1114 to 1118 Locust St) and Waverly (1127 to 1131 Waverly St) as separate gardens, so the Waverly and Sartain alias names may belong to other records. Needs review. Neighborhood is left out because the sources do not show whether this address is inside the Washington Square West boundary. The Love Your Park listing for May 9, 2026 does not say whether the day is open to the public.

records.name: We Are the Seeds
records.summary: A Native-led Philadelphia project that shares and teaches Indigenous arts and cultures. It runs the Seeds Philly weekend, a podcast, and an Indigenous listening garden in West Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Go to a Seeds Philly weekend when one is held, listen to the group's podcast, or ask the group to bring an Indigenous arts workshop to your school or organization.

schedule.text: Seeds Philly has been a yearly weekend of talks, live art, films and workshops. The listening garden has no posted hours.

locations.label: Indigenous listening garden, West Philadelphia (street address not published)

cost.text: Festival tickets are pay what you can, with a suggested donation of $20.

first_step.how: Ask the group, through its website, to bring a workshop to your school or organization. Watch its site and Instagram for news about a future Seeds Philly weekend.
first_step.basis: The festival was open to the public, but organizers say it may not return for the foreseeable future, and the garden has no published address or hours.
first_step.what_to_expect: Seeds Philly is a two-day weekend with talks, live painting, short films, workshops and an Indigenous art show. The 2026 festival was held at Cherry Street Pier in September. In September 2026, organizers told the Inquirer it may be the last Seeds Philly for the foreseeable future because the money has run out.
first_visit_tips: Check with the group before you plan a trip, since the festival's future is uncertain.
The listening garden's street address and hours are not published, so ask the group before you visit.
Follow the group on Instagram or read its Substack for updates.

records.notes: The EIN 061748326 from the IRS lead is left out of match. The group's site says it is a project of CultureTrust Greater Philadelphia. The sponsor's own page calls the organization CultureWorks Greater Philadelphia and does not list an EIN, so the EIN may belong to the sponsor. Check before using it. The Inquirer report says organizers may not run the festival for the foreseeable future, but the group's site also describes a fundraising appeal for its 10th year (a $10,000 goal) and a 2027 theater piece, so the group itself appears to continue. The group's gardens page returned 404, so the listening garden's address and hours remain unknown.
